page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance powered by AWS Graviton2 processors built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical CPU cores operating at 2.5 GHz with one thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 512 GB DDR4, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. A key hardware differentiator is the inclusion of 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage alongside a 25 Gbps baseline networking interface, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute performance, highlighted by a multi-core stress-ng score of 97,055.96 and a Clang compilation score of 43,022 in Geekbench. Cached memory throughput reaches 3,780.5 GB/sec on small block reads, while Redis SET performance achieves 72.91 million operations per second and static web serving delivers 45.28 GB/sec throughput. Conversely, single-threaded execution is comparatively modest, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 978 and single-threaded gzip compression at 20.36 GB/sec. Large model CPU-only LLM inference speeds remain limited, generating 2.77 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model.

The presence of 512 GB RAM paired with 3,800 GB of low-latency NVMe scratch storage offers substantial resource density for high-throughput I/O and in-memory operations. Because the Graviton2 processor utilizes dedicated single-threaded cores without simultaneous multithreading, workloads benefit from predictable core isolation. AWS r6gd.16xlarge is well positioned for memory-intensive and local I/O-heavy production environments, including in-memory databases like Redis, distributed caching layers, large relational database engines, high-concurrency web services, and big data ETL processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated physical cores on the ARM64 AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz. It includes 512 GB of system memory, 3,800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, and a 25 Gbps baseline network link managed by the Nitro hypervisor. Benchmark data shows top-tier multi-threaded compute capability, high cached memory bandwidth, and strong throughput in Redis operations (72.91 million ops/sec) and web serving (45.28 GB/sec). Single-threaded tasks and CPU-based LLM generation display lower performance characteristics. With an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and bundled local NVMe storage, this instance is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, key-value stores, distributed data caches, and ETL data processing workloads.
